title: Source licence register
description: Governs content/sources/registry.yaml. Every source cited anywhere in the corpus must appear here. The register — not the schema and not the author — decides what may be quoted from a given document, so a change in a publisher's terms is a data change rather than a code change. Changes to this file require steward approval (see GOVERNANCE.md).

designation.description: How practitioners refer to it. Example: ISO/IEC 17025:2017, JCGM 100:2008, ASME Y14.5-2018.

edition.description: Default edition assumed by citations that do not override it. Cite against a specific edition always — clause numbering moves between editions.

tier.description: 1 = verbatim quotation permitted (freely licensed or public-domain sources). 2 = fully referenceable, bounded quotation only. 3 = reference only, no quotation whatsoever; the reader consults their own licensed copy. When a source's terms are unclear, it is Tier 3 — the project's default posture is conservative.

quotation.description: Machine-enforced quotation limits. The validator reads these; nothing else may relax them.

maxWordsPerQuote.description: Hard cap per individual quotation. Omit only when permitted is false.

maxQuotesPerElement.description: Hard cap on quotations from this source within a single element.

requiresCommentary.description: When true, a quotation must be accompanied by the author's own commentary. Enforces quotation-for-commentary rather than quotation-as-substitute.

strippedInRedistributable.description: When true, quote text from this source is removed by `npm run build:bok --strip-tier2` and replaced with a pointer to the clause. Citations are never stripped.

blockedPendingCounsel.description: When true, no quotation may be authored against this source regardless of the limits above, because legal review of its terms is not complete. The limits stay recorded so they take effect the moment counsel reports — this is a gate, not a revision of them. Set on every entry whose `notes` carry CONFIRM-WITH-COUNSEL; that marker is prose and enforces nothing on its own.

access.description: How a reader obtains the document. Recorded so that a Tier 3 citation can tell someone where to go.

termsBasis.description: The documented reason for this tier classification: publisher terms of use, licence text, statutory status such as a US Government work, or recorded legal advice. A tier assignment without a stated basis is not reviewable and will be rejected.

supersedes.description: Earlier editions this entry replaces. Superseded editions remain in the register — existing citations against them must keep resolving.
